features.title: Decision routing to an action plan

features.title: Backoff, 429 pause and permanent errors

features.title: Circuit breaker and global kill switch
features.description: A temporary ban, logout or repeated 429s open the breaker so only P0 lockdowns run (configurable), the operator is alerted, detections continue for later cleanup, and a global pause stops all actions.

features.title: Silent mode enforced at the queue

features.title: Hourly ban cap, deletion circuit and kill switches

features.title: .set, .get and .settings by dotted key
features.description: `.set <key> <value>` validates with the same schema as the API and writes history and audit; `.get <key>` and `.settings` show values, with errors explained in the admin's language.

features.title: Friendly settings commands, .autoban and .askadmins
features.description: .status, .mode, .preset, .silent, .newsignal, .policy, .block/.allow/.blocknew, .autoban <type> … and .askadmins change the same dotted keys as .set; .preset resets the matrix and `.autoban … auto ai` is refused until a track record exists.

features.title: .ban, .kick, .unban, .allow, .unallow, .undo
features.description: `.ban` requires a reason spam|other (asking, and defaulting to other), `.kick` kicks without a rejoin block, `.unban` lifts a local ban, `.allow/.unallow` manage the member allow-list, and `.undo` reverses the bot's last reversible action in the group.

features.title: .domain and .word with dry-run counts
features.description: `.domain allow|block` and `.word block|unblock` edit group lists, and `.word block` first replies with how many recent messages (72 h inbox, in memory) it would have matched.

features.title: Inbound-first onboarding by DM
features.description: A START DM gets the three setup steps; when the bot is promoted it DMs the promoting admin only if they have an open thread, otherwise waits; a not-admin group gets at most one reminder per day in an existing thread; a group invite link sent by an admin is joined only after checking they admin it.

features.title: Review items with short codes
features.description: Routes that ask admins create reviews (kind, subject, proposed action, deadline, on_timeout) with a unique short code such as K7Q2, and dashboard is the default destination.

features.title: Review group destination
features.description: `.reviewgroup here` in a separate non-protected group sets it as the destination (a protected group is refused), `.reviewgroup off` clears it, one review group can serve several groups, and the bot warns when it contains non-admins.

features.title: End-to-end fast lane: inbox to actions
features.description: An inbox message flows through envelope, normalization, T0/T1 analyzers, scoring and routing into detections and enqueued actions in one transaction; end-to-end tests with the fake client show known spam from a max-trust member is deleted and sent to admins, and from a new member deleted and banned under Standard.

features.title: Replay harness for inbox events and fixtures
features.description: A replay command and test helper feed stored inbox rows or fixture events through the full pipeline with the fake client and report verdicts, so rule changes can be compared; CI runs the replay tests.

features.title: Golden envelope tests from spike fixtures
features.description: Each spike fixture under testdata/fixtures/ produces an envelope that matches its golden file, including status, group-status and broadcast shapes.

features.title: docker-compose.yml, .env.example, README and CONTRIBUTING
features.description: `docker compose up -d` starts bot + postgres with healthchecks, .env.example documents every variable, and README (unofficial-client ban risk), CONTRIBUTING (development with the fake WAClient) and CODE_OF_CONDUCT exist.

features.description: An OpenAI-compatible adapter works with hosted APIs and Ollama/llama.cpp/vLLM/LM Studio via base_url, using native schema when available and JSON mode otherwise.

features.title: Context bundle from the 72 h inbox
features.description: With ai.context on, the request includes the replied-to message, up to N=5 previous messages in 10 minutes, group info and allowed-content summary, sender context and existing replies, redacted, capped at ~2,000 characters and fenced as untrusted data; nothing new is stored.

features.title: AI budgets and metrics
features.description: ai_usage tracks calls and tokens per group and day; budgets send uncertain items straight to admins when exhausted (never deleting) with an 80% alert; metrics expose calls per 1,000 messages, cost, latency, cache hit rate, retries and unsure share.

features.title: AI result cache and one call per cluster
features.description: Results are cached on hash(normalized text + context hash + model + prompt version) for 30 days, and copies in the same SimHash cluster or campaign reuse the first verdict.

features.title: T3 verification of the UNCERTAIN band
features.description: Only UNCERTAIN messages go to the AI; spam ≥ ai.spam_confidence is deleted with the ban sent to admins, not spam ≥ 0.9 is logged, and unsure, low confidence, timeout, error or no AI configured go to admins with nothing deleted.
evidence: internal/ai/gateway: TestVerifyOutcomes, TestOnlyUncertainReachesTheAI, TestAIOffGoesToAdmins, TestBudgetExhaustedGoesToAdmins, TestPropertyOnlyConfidentAISpamDeletes

features.title: Early-AI safety: ai evidence never auto-bans without a track record
features.description: A ban resting on source ai routes to ask admins in every preset until the instance meets the track-record bar; property tests show AI-only evidence and looser near-duplicates never auto-ban.

features.title: Corpus entries, confirmations and learned rules
features.description: corpus_entries store redacted and normalized text, fingerprints, links, hashed numbers, media hashes and provenance; corpus_confirmations and learned_rules link entries to groups and rules; label is spam only.

features.title: Evidence snapshots for deletions and confirmed-spam capture
features.description: Every deletion keeps a redacted evidence snapshot (text + thumbnail) for 30 days, and spam an admin confirms (.spam, review ✅) is stored as a corpus entry so exact and near-duplicate matching can catch it next time.

features.title: Review message rendering and posting
features.description: Review items post as text (or the inline thumbnail with a caption) with who/what/why/score/source, third-party numbers and emails masked and text truncated to ~300 characters, and review_messages maps our message IDs to the review.

features.title: Reactions and reply keywords as votes
features.description: Reactions on a review message (✅👍 ban, ❌👎 not spam, removal withdraws) and replies quoting it (ban/kick/طرد/حظر, ok/not spam/ليس سبام, delete only, clear) become votes; `.review K7Q2 ban` and `.pending` work too.

features.title: Near-duplicate matching against the corpus (T1)
features.description: After the fingerprint allow-list check, SimHash ≤ 3 bits or MinHash ≥ 0.9 to a confirmed entry is CERTAIN known evidence and looser closeness is a rules signal that only sends the message to the AI.

features.title: Overturns retract confirmed spam and delete evidence text
features.description: Every not-spam decision (.notspam, review ❌, an overturned .spam or bot deletion) deletes the evidence-snapshot text, removes the strike and restores trust; if the message was confirmed spam, its corpus entry leaves the matching indexes at once (NOTIFY) and only a fingerprint allow-list entry, checked first by near-duplicate matching, is kept; tests cover both cases and assert no text of the overturned message remains.

features.title: Reply .spam and .notspam
features.description: Replying .spam deletes the message, bans the sender (allowed for established members because it's an admin decision) and records confirmed spam; .notspam/.ok restores trust, records the false positive and retracts what the confirmation added.

features.title: Admin-only, first-wins decisions
features.description: Only current admins of the protected group can decide; the first valid vote wins atomically even under concurrent votes; late voters get one 👌 and 'already handled'; every vote is stored; the decision executes through the normal action path.

features.title: Outcome edit or follow-up reply
features.description: A decided review message is edited to show who decided and what happened while within 20 minutes, and gets a quoting follow-up reply after that.

features.title: Review timeouts, fallbacks and .review commands
features.description: Pending reviews time out (6 h, or 15 min in ask_before_action) into keep_deleted_no_ban, delete_no_ban, auto_ban or dismiss, auto_ban refused in ask modes, for established members and hacked accounts; `.review group|dashboard` and `.review timeout …` configure it.

features.title: Blacklist table and number normalization
features.description: number_blacklist stores E.164 numbers with keyed hashes, scope and reason; input in international, local-with-default-country, 00-prefixed, Arabic-digit and wa.me forms normalizes correctly, several per command, and invalid numbers are reported.

features.title: .blacklist add/remove/list/check
features.description: Admins add, remove, list (masked except the last digits) and check numbers per group; the operator adds instance-wide entries with --instance; every change is audit-logged.

features.title: Blacklist identity resolution
features.description: Blacklisted numbers resolve to LIDs via batched GetUserInfo within the read budget, both identities link to the person, and numbers not on WhatsApp still work as content signals.

features.title: Blacklist enforcement
features.description: A blacklisted member is banned silently (admins never acted on, the adder told instead), a blacklisted joiner is kicked, their join requests rejected and messages deleted at P1; in ask-admins groups instance-wide entries become review items.

features.title: Blacklisted number in content is known spam
features.description: A blacklisted number in a vCard waid/TEL, a wa.me link or advertised in text is CERTAIN known evidence, and removing it from the list lifts the signal.

features.title: Membership history: join method, added-by, join-to-first-message
features.description: Every join records the method (invite link, added, approved, pre-existing), who added or approved, the first-message time and join-to-first-message seconds, and leaves record the reason.

features.title: Rule-pack YAML format with must/must-not-match tests
features.description: rules/packs/<name>.yaml packs (keywords, phrases, regexes, domains, numbers, hashes, metadata) load into global rules, and a test runs every pack against its own tests: block so a pack that hits normal phrasing fails CI.

features.title: Lockdown action (announce, join approval, invite reset)
features.description: A lockdown action sets announce mode and optionally join approval and resets the invite link through WAClient at P0, and an unlock action reverses announce and approval.

features.title: Backlog metrics and early lockdown
features.description: Metrics expose queue depth, wait time, rate vs ceiling and backlog ETA per group and bot; when a group's projected delete backlog exceeds 60 s it is locked at once and reopened after auto_lockdown_minutes or when the visible spam is gone, whichever is later.

features.title: .lockdown and .unlock
features.description: `.lockdown 15m` locks the group for the given time and `.unlock` reopens it early, both through the action queue.

features.title: Name and picture history for confirmed spammers
features.description: When someone is confirmed as a spammer, their push-name history and profile picture ID/hash are captured in name_history and profile_snapshots, and nothing is captured for ordinary members.

features.title: /api/v1 server with OpenAPI spec and operator tokens
features.description: The api role serves /api/v1 with a checked-in OpenAPI spec, consistent JSON errors and request IDs, authenticated for now by operator API tokens; a test fails when a route is missing from the spec.

features.title: Settings API with .set parity
features.description: GET/PATCH group settings by dotted key use the same validation, history and audit as `.set`, and a parity test changes every key through both paths.

features.title: API for groups, detections and reviews
features.description: The API lists groups with status, detections with explanations and reviews, and can decide a review, using the same decision path as WhatsApp.

features.title: Google (Gemini) adapter
features.description: A Google adapter classifies with structured output behind the same interface and config shape.

features.title: Learn only from confirmed spam
features.description: Review spam decisions, .spam, .ban spam and website confirmations create corpus entries; reason other never does; auto-kicks ≥ 0.98 with ≥ 2 families and auto_apply timeouts are provisional; an optional 'was it spam?' question for removals in the WhatsApp app learns only from a yes.

features.title: Group-scoped learned rules from confirmed spam
features.description: Confirmed URLs, domains, numbers, channels, invites, media hashes and SimHashes become group-scoped learned rules; globally allow-listed or top-site domains get a weighted signal and an operator suggestion instead.

features.title: Few-shot example selection without embeddings
features.description: Up to k≈4 redacted confirmed-spam examples are chosen by shared URLs/domains/numbers/channels/invites, then SimHash/MinHash closeness, then keywords, then campaign or category.

features.title: Overturns also retract learned rules
features.description: On top of the corpus retraction, an overturn removes the group-scoped learned rules the entry created (learned_rules).

features.title: Learning limits and admin reputation
features.description: Each admin adds at most 20 learned patterns per day and each group at most M (extras queue for the operator), young groups contribute provisional entries only, and admins whose decisions get overturned have later contributions marked provisional.

features.title: Recent-traffic check before activating a learned pattern
features.description: Before a learned pattern activates it is matched in memory against the group's 72 h inbox and message_index; one that would match more than x% of recent non-spam traffic is rejected with a reason, storing nothing extra.

features.title: Rollback by admin or group and burst alerts
features.description: The operator can revert everything learned from one admin or one group in one action, and a burst detector alerts on unusual spikes of learned patterns.

features.title: Corpus retention and group deletion
features.description: Corpus raw text expires after 180 days, fingerprints 180 days after their last hit, and a group's corpus is deleted when the bot leaves the group or the owner asks.

features.title: Property test: normal text is never stored
features.description: A test drives normal, overturned and AI-context messages through the pipeline and asserts no table outside the 72 h inbox gains their text.

features.title: Corpus import parsing and validation (JSONL/CSV)
features.description: `antispam corpus import` parses JSONL and CSV with the documented fields, defaults label to spam, reports rejected lines clearly, and `--dry-run` writes nothing; docs/CORPUS_FORMAT.md documents the format with synthetic examples.

features.title: Import: normalize, fingerprint, dedupe and store
features.description: Records are normalized and fingerprinted, deduped within the file and against the corpus, and stored as corpus entries with source import, the chosen scope and an import_batches row.

features.title: Cluster-aware hold-out split
features.description: A hold-out slice (default 20%) stratified by category and kind is split by cluster_id or computed near-duplicate cluster, so no cluster lands on both sides, and stored in eval_corpus.

features.title: Ham records in memory only, and undoing an import
features.description: Ham records are never stored as text, only used for an in-memory false-positive report and optional allow-list fingerprints; `antispam corpus remove --import <id>` removes every entry, fingerprint and learned rule of a batch.

features.title: Recall on the hold-out per band and type
features.description: An eval command replays the hold-out through the full pipeline and reports the share caught per band (CERTAIN, AI-verified, sent to admins, missed), type and preset, with a diff between rule versions; CI fails when recall drops.

features.title: Model comparison on the hold-out
features.description: The eval command runs several configured providers/models on the hold-out and reports recall, unsure share, cost and latency side by side.

features.title: Shadow-mode review and precision report
features.description: Would-be actions in shadow mode are reviewable, each review outcome counts toward precision per band, source and type, and a summary ('this week we would have deleted 42 messages and banned 3 people') is produced.

features.title: Bounded media decoding and media_cache
features.description: Thumbnails and images decode in a bounded worker pool with size, pixel and time limits (decompression bombs rejected), and results are cached by SHA256 in media_cache.

features.title: Thumbnail pHash/dHash with a BK-tree
features.description: Inline thumbnails get pHash/dHash, a BK-tree finds known-spam hashes within distance, ≤ 4 is CERTAIN known and looser is a rules signal.

features.title: Profile fetch and cache
features.description: Profile snapshots (about text, picture ID/hash, verified name) are fetched with batched UserInfo and ExistingID picture checks within the read budget, cached 24 h and invalidated by Picture/UserAbout events.

features.title: Business profile description and website via raw IQ
features.description: The adapter reads the business profile description and website (raw IQ or upstream patch, as confirmed in the spike) in addition to whatsmeow's parsed fields.

features.title: Profile scanning analyzer
features.description: Push name, about, business description/website and picture hash are scanned on join and first message as weighted signals; members' own status posts and DM spam to the bot (including broadcasts) only lower that person's reputation.

features.title: SSRF-safe HTTP client
features.description: An HTTP client refuses private, link-local and metadata IPs (checked at dial time), caps redirects at 5, times out after 3 s and limits body size.

features.title: link_cache with positive and negative TTLs
features.description: Resolution results are cached by key with 24 h (invites/channels), 7 d (unshortened URLs) and 1 h negative TTLs.

features.title: Invite-link and channel resolution (T2)
features.description: Invite codes resolve via GroupInfoFromLink and channels via NewsletterInfo(+FromInvite) within the read budget and link cache; names, topics, descriptions, sizes, subscriber counts and verification feed signals.

features.title: wa.me link resolution
features.description: wa.me/message, wa.me/qr and wa.me/<phone> links resolve to the business name, pre-filled text or account, which feed the text and number pipelines.

features.title: Status attribution and reshare analysis
features.description: Attribution action URLs go to the URL analyzer, reshared channel JIDs to the channel analyzer, RESHARED_FROM_POST_MANY_TIMES is a mild signal, and a reply whose only payload is a spammy quoted status counts as spam.

features.title: Shortener expansion
features.description: Known shorteners are expanded with the SSRF-safe client (HEAD then GET), and the final target goes through the URL analyzer.

features.title: URLhaus/OpenPhish feeds and optional Safe Browsing
features.description: A River job refreshes URLhaus and OpenPhish into the domain/URL reputation tables, and Google Safe Browsing/Web Risk is checked when a key is configured.

features.title: Domain age (RDAP) and look-alike domains
features.description: RDAP registration dates (cached 1–7 days) make very new domains a weighted signal, and hosts whose confusable skeleton matches a protected brand or that are close to an allow-listed domain add a weighted signal.

features.title: Verdict cache by envelope fingerprint
features.description: Verdicts are cached by text-free envelope fingerprint for 7 days, and clean verdicts are purged when the rule-set version changes.

features.title: Cross-group campaign signal
features.description: The same SimHash, sticker hash, channel, number or domain appearing across groups or senders within a window adds a weighted campaign signal in every opted-in group.

features.title: Behaviour signals: floods, mentions, forwards, join-then-post
features.description: Counters emit weighted signals for floods, mass mentions, high forwarding scores, post-then-self-delete, reaction floods, posting within seconds of joining and the same fingerprint from one sender in ≥ k groups.

features.title: Join-raid response
features.description: ≥ 8 joins in 2 minutes with ≥ 3 suspicious profiles turns on join approval, resets the invite link, kicks suspicious joiners in capped batches within the hourly cap, sends the rest as one review item and alerts admins.

features.title: Message-flood response
features.description: Many senders posting near-duplicates triggers early announce mode, batched bans and newest-first cleanup, with automatic reopening and one alert in the review destination.

features.title: Optional warn/mute/ban ladder with strikes
features.description: With ladder.enabled, strikes within the window step through the configured actions for new/unknown senders, replacing the matrix's auto_ban for early strikes; established members still go to admins; the ladder is inert when disabled (property test).

features.title: Mute emulation and .mute/.unmute
features.description: A muted member's new messages are deleted at P1, a flooding muted member escalates to a ban, warnings are DM or in-group only as configured, and .mute/.unmute work only with the ladder on.

features.title: Join-request detection
features.description: Join requests are detected by parsing GroupInfo.UnknownChanges (shape from the spike) or by polling GetGroupRequestParticipants for approval-mode groups.

features.title: Join screening
features.description: A profile scan runs on every join and join request and only feeds the score or opens a join-screening review.

features.title: Join-approval autopilot (opt-in)
features.description: With autopilot on, clean requesters are approved, obvious spam profiles rejected in batches, and the rest left for humans.

features.title: Edit re-analysis
features.description: An edit is fully re-analysed against the original message ID, a benign-to-spam edit adds a signal, and deletion uses the original ID.

features.title: View-once and undecryptable policy
features.description: View-once from new or untrusted members can be blocked by policy and deleted by ID, and the matrix's view_once cell applies; content is never inspected.

features.title: Per-person activity baselines
features.description: activity_stats keeps each person's hour-of-day histogram, median interval, cross-group burst maximum and totals, updated incrementally.

features.title: Possibly-compromised signal family
features.description: Cross-group bursts, first-ever links or contacts, campaign content, unusual hours, bursts after silence and profile change before spam are detected against the member's own history; two signals, or one plus known spam, mark a compromise event.

features.title: Hacked-account review
features.description: A compromise event deletes the spam and opens a 'may be hacked' review; there is never an automatic ban, strike, spammer profile, person learning or network ban (property test); for admins it only alerts.

features.title: Restriction while pending, .restrict and .clear
features.description: With restrict_while_pending on, the member's links/media/forwards are deleted everywhere until decided; .restrict/.restricted manage manual restrictions; .clear, a clear reply or the API closes the review without a ban and lifts restrictions.

features.title: DM reviewers with opt-in
features.description: `.reviewers add/remove` chooses reviewers, each must opt in once (REVIEWER code link, login or `.reviewer on`), pending reviewers get nothing, and `.review dm` sends items by DM; votes must come from chosen reviewers.

features.title: Review destination fallback chain
features.description: If the destination is unusable (no active reviewers, bot removed from the review group), items go dm → group → dashboard and the owner is told once.

features.title: Quiet hours, digests and per-reviewer caps
features.description: Quiet hours delay DMs without stopping timeouts, a daily digest can replace per-item messages, more than 10 review DMs per hour fold into a digest with 'all ok / all spam', and updates to more than 3 other reviewers are batched.

features.title: Confirm-before-kick option
features.description: With confirm-before-kick on, a ban decision by one admin waits for confirmation (or the dashboard) before the kick executes.

features.title: Precision report at the delete threshold
features.description: The eval tooling reports precision at T_delete from reviewed shadow and live decisions per type, the phase 2 exit metric.

features.title: Dashboard users, sessions and CSRF
features.description: Sessions are opaque random IDs in HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax cookies stored hashed in Postgres with a 30-day sliding expiry, 'log out other devices' works, and cookie-authenticated writes need a CSRF token.

features.title: Login by messaging the bot
features.description: The login page shows a code and a wa.me link with LOGIN <code>; when the bot receives that DM from the matching number, the waiting browser (SSE or polling) is logged in.

features.title: Outbound OTP login with eligibility check
features.description: A code is sent only to numbers that admin a protected group or are operators; only an HMAC is stored with 5-minute TTL and 5 attempts bound to the browser; per-number, per-IP and global rate limits and lockout apply.

features.title: Permissions: admins, owners and operators
features.description: Requests check current admin status (refreshing a cache older than 10 minutes), owners can change everything, an owner-only lock is honoured, operators come from OPERATOR_PHONES, and non-browser clients use short-lived API tokens with explicit CORS for other origins.

features.title: HSTS, CSP and fail2ban-friendly logs
features.description: Responses carry HSTS and a strict CSP, auth failures produce fail2ban-friendly log lines, and the operator area can be limited by IP.

features.title: Settings preview API
features.description: Before saving, a settings change can be replayed against the last week's detections to report how many decisions it would change.

features.title: Frontend app scaffold (framework chosen by a human first)
features.description: Once a human records the framework choice (open question 16), a separate mobile-first, RTL-aware Arabic/English frontend app builds in CI and its static output is served same-origin by the Go binary.

features.title: Website login pages
features.description: The website offers tap-to-message login by default with the OTP fallback, works on a phone and shows clear errors and lockouts.

features.title: My groups and group overview pages
features.description: Admins see their groups with status and today's stats, a detection timeline with explanations, undo buttons and charts, and the activity/audit log for their groups.

features.title: Protection settings page
features.description: Preset picker, auto-ban grid with an advanced evidence column, ask-admins switch, content rules in plain language, just-joined toggle and ladder, each change previewed before saving.

features.title: Lists page with dry-run
features.description: Allowed members, domain lists, blocked words with a test box showing dry-run matches, and global pack subscriptions are editable.

features.title: Reviews and notifications settings page
features.description: The destination picker, reviewer checkboxes with opt-in status, review-group instructions and warnings, timeout/fallback, quiet hours, reaction mapping and a sample review preview.

features.title: Review queue and history pages
features.description: Open items can be decided (ban / not spam / delete only) with masked evidence, closing them in WhatsApp too; history filters by group, decider and outcome and shows later overturns.

features.title: Learned patterns and blacklist pages
features.description: Each group sees what learning added with provenance, hit counts and one-click retract, and manages blacklisted numbers (masked) with the same rules as the commands.

features.title: Website and command parity test
features.description: A test changes every setting exposed on the website through the `.set` path and asserts identical stored documents and audit entries.

features.title: Onboarding on the website
features.description: Waiting and not-admin groups are shown with next steps, admins choose a review destination, and an optional 24 h shadow first run sends its summary to the review destination.

features.title: Operator pages: pairing, health, queue, budgets, kill switch
features.description: Operators pair numbers by QR or code on the website, see bot health and ban status, queue depth, AI spend, global packs and promotion queue, change the ceiling (marked risky, audited) and use the kill switch.

features.title: Group offboarding deletes its data
features.description: When the bot leaves a group (or the owner asks), the group's settings, corpus, reviews and member data are deleted per the retention rules.

features.title: Template privacy notice
features.description: A template privacy notice explains what is stored, why, for how long and how to appeal or request deletion, naming the configured AI provider, and is linked from onboarding, the about text and the website.

features.title: docs/SELF_HOSTING.md
features.description: The guide covers requirements, compose up, operator login, pairing, adding the bot, reverse proxy examples (Caddy/Traefik/nginx/Coolify), backups, upgrades, privacy and ban-risk advice.

features.title: Synthetic load generator
features.description: A generator replays synthetic events at 10× expected peak and reports CPU, memory, inbox lag and queue behaviour on ARM64.

features.title: Staging release checklist (human-run)
features.description: A scripted checklist for a second number in a private test group covers every message type, delete/kick, edits, raid simulation and login, to run before each release and whatsmeow bump.

features.title: Release with the website and self-hosting guide
features.description: A release that ships the website is cut through the release workflow, with release notes and the README pointing at the self-hosting guide.

features.title: Vision tier (T4) for images and stickers
features.description: Images, stickers and thumbnails go to a configured vision adapter only when visual evidence decides and cheaper tiers are inconclusive, within the AI budgets.

features.title: Vision on profile pictures
features.description: Ambiguous profile pictures can be classified by the vision tier, as a weighted signal only.

features.title: 'Unrelated groups' definition
features.description: Two groups are unrelated when owners differ, member overlap is under 20%, they aren't in the same community and the deciding admins differ; shared by promotion and network quorum.

features.title: Global promotion of learned patterns
features.description: A pattern confirmed in ≥ 3 unrelated groups within 30 days is promoted to global for opted-in groups, high-impact types need operator approval, and overturns from ≥ 2 unrelated groups demote it and alert the operator.

features.title: Weekly bounded re-weighting
features.description: A weekly job refits signal weights by logistic regression on decided reviews, limits each change to ±20%, applies it only if the overturn rate doesn't rise and hold-out recall doesn't drop, needs operator approval for global changes, and uses per-group offsets only with ≥ 50 labels.

features.title: Track record and opt-in for ai auto-bans
features.description: The instance tracks decisions per deciding source; once ai has ≥ 200 decisions with ≥ 98% confirmed over 30 days plus shadow precision, an operator or admin may explicitly add ai to matrix cells; it never happens automatically.

features.title: Appeals end to end
features.description: A DM 'appeal' (or any DM from someone banned) starts an appeal routed as a review; approval lifts the ban, clears strikes, sets a temporary allow-list and sends an invite in the existing thread; appeals.notify_removed (off by default) DMs removed people once.

features.title: /appeal page
features.description: A public /appeal page explains the process and opens the inbound wa.me appeal flow.

features.title: Overturn-rate dashboard and auto-disable
features.description: Overturn rates per rule, source and group are shown, and rules above the configured overturn rate are disabled automatically with an operator alert.

features.title: Per-rule shadow deployment
features.description: A new rule or weight set can run in shadow on live traffic, recording its would-be effect without acting.

features.title: Organisations
features.description: Groups join an organisation by same owner, same community (linked parent / subgroups) or an admin-of-all link on the website, stored in organisations and group_orgs.

features.title: Network scope settings and .network
features.description: network.contribute and network.enforce (off/org/all) are settable by website and `.network off|org|all`; `.network` shows bans affecting the group and pending identity matches.

features.title: Network candidates and risk signal
features.description: A spam ban that doesn't meet the network rule records a candidate, and other in-scope groups get a strong risk signal (stricter thresholds, join-screening review) but no automatic kick.

features.title: Network quorum rule and protections
features.description: A network ban activates only for human-confirmed spam meeting (a) score ≥ 0.97 with ≥ 2 families, (b) confirmation in ≥ 2 unrelated groups in 30 days, or (c) operator decision, and never for admins anywhere, established members elsewhere, flagged admins or past the per-admin daily limit; each negative case is tested.

features.title: Operator approval queue for network bans
features.description: Candidates that need the operator (automatic kicks without human confirmation, admins, established members) wait in an approval queue the operator can approve or reject.

features.title: Network-ban job and prioritized child actions
features.description: An active ban plans one job with prioritized child actions per in-scope group (P0/P1/P2/P4), idempotent by (ban, group, action), and every step is recorded in network_actions and audit_log, visible to operators and per group to admins.

features.title: Identity-pending watch rules
features.description: When a group uses an identifier not yet linked, the ban becomes a watch rule that applies the first time the person appears there (join, message, participant refresh) or when the identity resolves.

features.title: Re-scan recorded messages, delete only spam
features.description: The person's recorded messages from the last 72 h go back through the pipeline with the ban evidence; only those sharing a fingerprint, touching the campaign or scoring ≥ T_delete are deleted, the rest are kept, and 2–30-day-old matches are listed as too old to delete.

features.title: Rejoin kicks and join-request rejection
features.description: A network-banned joiner in an in-scope group is kicked at P0 (batched in raids), matching join requests are rejected, and in ask-admins groups an incoming ban becomes a review item.

features.title: Admin re-add override
features.description: When a current admin deliberately re-adds a network-banned person (not via invite link), the bot allow-lists them in that group, doesn't kick, and tells the admins once with an undo.

features.title: Network-ban report
features.description: The originating group gets one summary (kicked, deleted, kept, too old, skipped) and each affected group a digest line with the reason category and an undo.

features.title: Network-wide unban
features.description: An upheld appeal, the operator or the sole contributing group lifts the ban everywhere: cancels pending actions, removes rejoin blocks, restores trust, retracts learned patterns and the spammer profile, notifies groups and sends invite links in the person's own thread.

features.title: Network ban across 40 groups within pacing
features.description: A synctest scenario bans a person across 40 groups with batched kicks and re-scans, finishing within pacing limits without exceeding the ceiling or per-group caps.

features.title: Spammer profiles
features.description: Confirmed spammers (never possibly-hacked accounts) get a profile linking identities, names, snapshots, group footprint, content and timing; ordinary members never do.

features.title: Campaign graph
features.description: Accounts and artifacts (domains, number hashes, channels, picture hashes, SimHash clusters, invites) form a graph whose components above a threshold become campaigns, and new accounts touching one get a campaign prior.

features.title: Nightly intelligence patterns with lift
features.description: A nightly job computes number-prefix clusters, picture and name reuse, shared artifacts, join-to-spam timing and repeat inviters against the base rate of legitimate members, keeping only high-lift, well-supported patterns.

features.title: Capped identity-prior signals
features.description: Priors add at most +1.0 combined and +0.3 for number prefix, never count as a signal family, never act alone (property test), are per-group switchable, and a prefix signal with rising overturns disables itself.

features.title: Spammer views for group admins
features.description: Group admins see only spammers from their groups and their groups' data, with cross-group counts; every view is written to intel_access_log and there is no bulk export.

features.title: Operator intelligence views
features.description: Operators search by name, number, LID, domain or picture similarity, see timelines, the campaign view, patterns with lift and switches, and the network-ban queue.

features.title: Intelligence retention jobs
features.description: Expiry jobs delete (not hide) spammer profiles 12 months after last activity unless banned, keep 10 snapshots per person, and delete non-spammer membership history after 30 days.

features.title: Column-level encryption for identity data
features.description: Photos and identity fields are encrypted at rest with a key held outside the database, and the optional encrypted review thumbnail (off by default) expires after 30 days.

features.title: Upheld appeals and deletion requests delete intelligence
features.description: An upheld appeal deletes the person's profile, snapshots, names, campaign links, stats and corpus, keeping a minimal audit with a keyed hash; a 'delete my data' DM goes to the operator and is honoured within 7 days unless tied to an active justified ban.

features.title: Signed feed format
features.description: Rule-pack and fingerprint feeds are versioned files signed with the publisher's key, containing no message text, names, photos or identities.

features.title: Subscribe to feeds
features.description: Operators subscribe to feeds over HTTPS; imported entries are weighted signals only, never hard blocks or network bans, unless the operator promotes them.

features.title: Publish feeds
features.description: An operator can publish their promoted rules and hashed fingerprints as a signed feed.

features.title: Multiple bot numbers
features.description: Several numbers run in one deployment, each group is assigned to the bot that is admin there, and each bot keeps its own serial executor and pacing.

features.title: Primary and standby bots per group
features.description: With two bots in a group the primary acts and the standby reads, taking over when the primary loses admin or is banned; onboarding suggests the least-loaded number and the operator can migrate a group.

features.title: Failover during a temporary ban
features.description: When a bot is temp-banned its groups' actions re-route to a standby in the same group, otherwise wait for the ban to expire within their deadlines.

features.title: -media image with ffmpeg, libwebp and tesseract
features.description: A second Debian-slim image tag runs media workers that call ffmpeg/libwebp/tesseract as resource-limited subprocesses.

features.title: Animated sticker frames and video keyframes
features.description: Animated stickers get a first-frame pHash and OCR, and videos get ffmpeg keyframes for pHash and the vision tier.

features.title: OCR into the text pipeline
features.description: Image text and PDF first pages are OCR'd and the text goes through normalization and the text analyzers.

features.title: Optional voice transcription
features.description: Voice notes can be transcribed (opt-in) and analysed as text, within budgets.

features.title: External HTTP analyzer interface
features.description: An optional external analyzer receives a redacted envelope over HTTP/JSON and returns signals within a timeout, treated as T2-level and off by default.

features.title: Multi-node operation
features.description: Analysis workers and the web server run statelessly on several nodes, with Valkey/Redis for shared hot caches when there is more than one node.

features.title: Monthly partitioning
features.description: inbox, detections and message_index are partitioned by month and retention drops whole partitions.

features.title: Optional OpenTelemetry tracing
features.description: With tracing on, each message gets spans through the tiers; it's off by default.
